subject: chemistry
title: Le Chatelier Loop: Stress and Response
welcome_lead: Predict how systems respond when concentration, pressure or T shifts.
meta_desc: A-Level chemistry adventure on Le Chatelier's principle.
final_note: You can now nudge equilibria with precision.

concepts.def: System shifts to oppose imposed change.
Increase shifts to fewer gas moles.
At constant V no shift; constant P shifts.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Increasing pressure favours the side with fewer moles of gas. Equal moles -> no shift.

Example: N2(g) + 3H2(g) <-> 2NH3(g) (4 mol -> 2 mol). High pressure pushes forward, raising NH3 yield (Haber process).

Only T changes Kc. Endothermic reaction: increasing T raises Kc. Exothermic: increases T lowers Kc.

For the Haber process (exothermic forward), high T lowers yield but raises rate -> compromise at ~400 deg C with Fe catalyst.

Catalysts lower activation energy for both directions equally. They reduce time to reach equilibrium but do not shift it.

Position and Kc are independent of catalyst presence.

mcqs.q: Adding heat to an exothermic reaction shifts.
options: Backward (reverse)
Forward
No change
Catalyses forward

mcqs.q: A catalyst does what to Kc?
options: Leaves Kc unchanged
Increases Kc
Decreases Kc
Reverses sign

mcqs.q: Does a catalyst affect the position of equilibrium?
options: The system shifts to amplify the change because reactions always proceed in the disturbed direction.
A catalyst shifts the equilibrium towards the products.
No — it speeds up both the forward and reverse reactions equally, so equilibrium is reached faster but at the same position.
A catalyst increases the yield by being consumed in the forward reaction only.

mcqs.q: When a stress shifts an equilibrium, does the system fully undo the change?
options: The system shifts to completely cancel the change and return concentrations to their original values.
A catalyst increases the yield by being consumed in the forward reaction only.
No — Le Chatelier's principle says the system PARTIALLY opposes the change; equilibrium shifts to a new position that minimises but doesn't eliminate the disturbance.
The system shifts to amplify the change because reactions always proceed in the disturbed direction.

mcqs.q: Does adding a catalyst change the value of Kc?
options: No — a catalyst speeds up forward and reverse reactions equally, so Kc is unchanged.
A catalyst decreases Kc by stabilising the reactants.
The system shifts to amplify the change because reactions always proceed in the disturbed direction.
A catalyst increases Kc by favouring product formation.
